transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I'm having some trouble at work. I supervise a retail team, and lately, when I try to explain the inventory numbers or go over the weekend schedule, my words just start jumping around. I'll go from talking about the delivery trucks to Thursdays, and then somehow I'm on about the church grill or my boss’s tone. My team just looks at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying at all. It's been making things pretty difficult.
Have you noticed a decreased need for sleep lately, such as feeling fully rested after only a couple of hours?
No, I wouldn't say that. I sleep about the same as I always do. I definitely don't feel rested if I only get a couple of hours. I need my regular night's sleep.
Have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, depression, or a loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel depressed or sad. I still like doing the things I usually do when I'm not at work... it's just the trouble I'm having when I try to talk to my team that's bothering me. But my mood itself is fine.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

No, I haven't. I don't hear voices or... sounds that aren't really there. My hearing is perfectly normal. It's really just that issue with my words getting all mixed up when I try to explain things to my team.
How long have you been noticing this issue with your words jumping around?

I'd say it's been about six months now. That's when I really started noticing the jumbled explanations and... well, making these odd stops when I'm out on the sales floor trying to talk to the staff. It's been pretty noticeable for about half a year.
Have you ever felt that people were watching you, monitoring you, or plotting to harm you?

No, nothing like that. I don't feel like anyone is watching me or... trying to harm me. My team is good, and I don't have any suspicions about them or anyone else. It's really just my own frustration with my words getting tangled up, not anything to do with people plotting against me.
Could you tell me more about what you mean by making those 'odd stops' on the sales floor?

Well, it's... sometimes I'll be out on the floor, and I just sort of get stuck. Like, I'll catch myself pacing up and down the exact same aisle, or I'll just stand there straightening the same row of batteries over and over again. And other times, I'll have the schedule clipboard right in my hand, and I'll just stand there, completely stopped, while the associates are all looking at me, waiting for me to tell them what they need to be doing. I just kind of freeze up doing these repetitive things instead of actually managing the floor.
